newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SBC sees 10 pct Euro/US stocks correction.
newsitem.headline: SBC sees 10 pct Euro/US stocks correction.

text.p: A senior Swiss Bank Corp investment adviser said he thought stock exchanges in Europe and the United States could drop an average 10 percent from their highs in a correction from overvalued levels.

"I would not be surprised by a correction in the average magnitude of around 10 percent from highs," Burkhard Poschadel, leader of SBC's investment consulting, told the Finanz und Wirtschaft weekly in an interview published on Saturday.
"I cite this number because share market are overvalued by around this extent," he added.

He said corporate profits were below the long-term growth trend in Europe but above it in the United States, so that European bourses, especially in Germany and Britain, had more potential than U.S. stock markets.
He said SBC had reduced the percentage of shares in its investment straegy in November, but gave no more details.
Poschadel said investors had to expect smaller gains from stocks next year than in 1996.

"Thus for the time being we will stick to our underweighting in stock markets. But we will keep a part in shares as a long-term strategic investment and in Switzerland, for example, count on the pharmaceutical sector and selected insurance stocks," he said.
But he cautioned uncertainty about Europe's single currency project could still push up the Swiss franc temporarily. This tends to hurt the Swiss economy.
British shares are relatively fairly valued, he said.
Emerging markets also offer interesting possibilities because shares there are more favourably valued and stand to profit form above-average long-term economic growth rates.
